source_evidence: International investing can be more expensive than investing in U.S. companies. Markets outside the U.S. may have lower trading volumes and fewer listed companies than U.S. markets.
question: Misconception: International investments cost no more than U.S. investments, and foreign markets are always just as liquid.
answer: International investing can be more expensive than investing in U.S. companies. Also, markets outside the U.S. may have lower trading volumes and fewer listed companies, so liquidity can differ from that of U.S. markets. These are possibilities, not claims that every international investment has higher costs or lower liquidity.
